entries.name: DCF77 — time signal
entries.notes: 77.5 kHz from Mainflingen: the amplitude-keyed code every German radio clock listens to, one bit a second.

entries.name: CB channels 41–80
entries.notes: Germany licenses 80 CB channels rather than the CEPT 40; 41–80 are FM only.

entries.name: 4 m amateur
entries.notes: A 30 kHz secondary allocation, CW and SSB only — a sliver next to the UK's 500 kHz on the same band.

entries.name: BOS 4 m band
entries.notes: Legacy analogue public-safety radio. Largely migrated to BOS-Digitalfunk in 380–400 MHz, but fire brigades still run paging and fallback traffic here.

entries.name: UKW broadcast
entries.notes: The public and private FM networks, with RDS on essentially all of them.

entries.name: BOS 2 m band
entries.notes: Analogue public-safety VHF, and where POCSAG fire paging still runs.

entries.name: DAB+ — VHF Band III
entries.notes: The national ensemble sits on block 5C (178.352 MHz); the Länder ensembles fill the rest.

entries.name: BOS-Digitalfunk (TETRA)
entries.notes: The national public-safety TETRA network. Encrypted, so a scope shows the carriers and nothing else.
